name: signin_analyse
description: Read an Entra sign-in export (Graph signIns JSON, JSON Lines or CSV) or a Google Workspace login audit (Reports API activities, nested events one each; or CSV) offline and keep every record: id, correlation id, authentication details, applied conditional access policies, device and token context, the raw record and a locator (file, record, line, nested event). The format is read from the content. `status` and `status_basis` say whether every record was read; a malformed line, a record that is not a sign-in (a Workspace activity of another application included), a truncated gzip (every record before the break is kept), an archive (.zip, tar: named, not read) and a next-page marker are counted, located and listed. Time is not guessed: a time with no zone is refused unless assume_utc says it is UTC (recorded as an assumption), and a day/month/year string needs a date_order or unambiguous rows that prove one (a Date (UTC) column is UTC on its own say-so, but a day/month/year string in it is as ambiguous as in any other). `success` is true, false or null: a portal Status of Interrupted is null whatever the code beside it says, and a code the tool lists as a prompt in a sign-in flow (50074, 50076, 50079, 50125, 50140, 50158) is null with outcome_class interrupt, counted as `interrupts`, never in `failures` or in a burst. Accounts are told apart by their object id, else their lower-cased user name, never by a display name; `user` is a regex (at most 200 characters) matched against the user name and display name as printed, never against a withheld original; a pattern that can take exponential time is refused, and one test that takes more than a quarter of a second fails the call, named. An argument the tool does not have is refused, and a format that the content contradicts is refused. Leads, each a hypothesis bounded by the export (an empty list excludes nothing): single_factor_successes, failure_bursts_before_success (burst_min_failures or more consecutive failures within burst_window_seconds of a success, same account and application; every failure is listed, in burst_members past ten), prompts_before_success (prompt_min_count or more interrupted sign-ins in a row before a success: a lead for multi-factor prompt flooding, and what a slow user looks like), addresses_seen_once (once among this account's events in this export), impossible_travel (coordinates implying more than max_speed_kmh, successes at one recorded second far apart with no speed, or a country change within an hour without coordinates, marked coarse; the portal's `City, State, Country` string is split and its last component is the country). result is this tool's gloss; failure_reason is the provider's words. NOT measured: whether a sign-in was the account's owner, token use after sign-in, activity outside the supplied events. SENSITIVE: user names, addresses, locations and devices are in the answer; a field named or shaped like a credential is withheld and its original written only with write_values, in a job, to a mode 0600 file under $OUT: run as a job with secret_output: true when the case treats the export as sensitive. An out_file is never replaced by a smaller result; a read that ended early publishes it as <name>.partial<ext> and names it partial_records or partial_events, never complete_*, and SIGTERM leaves no temporary file.

path.description: One sign-in export: JSON, JSON Lines or CSV (the format is read from the content)

user.description: Case-insensitive regex (at most 200 characters) over the user name and display name as printed; a pattern that can take exponential time is refused

max_speed_kmh.description: Implied speed above which a pair of successes is flagged (default 900)

burst_window_seconds.description: Every failure of a burst must be within this many seconds of the success (default 3600)

burst_min_failures.description: Consecutive failures that make a burst (default 3); an interrupted sign-in is not a failure

prompt_min_count.description: Interrupted sign-ins in a row before a success, inside burst_window_seconds, that make a prompts_before_success lead (default 5)

assume_utc.description: Read a time that carries no zone as UTC. Say so only on the export's own documentation or collection record; the answer records the assumption

date_order.description: mdy or dmy, for day/month/year strings whose two leading fields are both 12 or less

format.description: auto (default: from the content), csv, json or jsonl; a format the content contradicts is refused

delimiter.description: CSV delimiter, one character (default a comma)

out_file.description: Optional JSONL path for every event, under the run directory (in a job, under $OUT: name it work/<your agent id>/..., which becomes $OUT). Never replaces a file already there: that one is kept and this one is named beside it

limit.description: Rows of each list returned inline (default 500, an inline page size); past it the whole list is in a file the answer names (under $OUT/tool-output in a job, work/<agent>/tool-output otherwise)

max_expanded_bytes.description: Most bytes read from one file after decompression (default 4 GiB); a file that reaches it is partial and says so

max_record_bytes.description: Most text held while one record is read (default 16 MiB); a larger record is rejected, located and listed, never cut

time_limit_seconds.description: Stop reading after this many seconds (default 540, at most 580); what was read is kept, the answer is partial and names the files not read

write_values.description: Write the originals of the values withheld from the answer to a mode 0600 file under $OUT. Honoured only when the tool runs as a job (run it with secret_output: true); outside a job it is refused and nothing is written
